videos.title: The Black Death Came on Ships — Europe Was Never the Same
videos.desc:
The Black Death killed half of Europe in six years — and it arrived on twelve ships. How the plague of 1347-1353 remade the world forever.

In the winter of 1349, villages stood empty, wheat rotted in the fields, and church bells rang for no one. This is the story of how a bacterium hiding in the fur of rats rode the Silk Road to a besieged port called Caffa, sailed to Sicily aboard twelve Genoese galleys, and then rewrote everything: wages, faith, medicine, and the place of women in the world. videos.title: The Ship That Couldn't Sink… Until It Did
videos.desc:
She was the grandest ship ever built — and the world swore she could never sink. This is the true story of the night arrogance met ice in the North Atlantic.

On April 14, 1912, the RMS Titanic struck an iceberg at 11:40 PM. Warnings ignored, a rescue ship asleep nineteen kilometers away, a band that played until the very end — and fifteen hundred souls lost in freezing water. This documentary follows the Titanic from her proud departure in Southampton to her final plunge at 2:20 AM, and the legacy that changed maritime law forever.

videos.title: 1816: The Year Summer Never Came
videos.desc:
Have you ever wondered how a mountain exploding on a tropical island could make it snow in July, half a world away? This is the story that has haunted me ever since I first heard it.

In April 1815, Mount Tambora erupted with the loudest sound in recorded human history, erasing two kingdoms and even a language. A year later, its ash veiled the sun, crops failed across the globe, and in a darkened Swiss villa, an eighteen-year-old girl dreamed of a monster called Frankenstein.

videos.title: Pompeii's Last Morning: A Living City Buried in 79 AD
videos.desc:
I have always been haunted by Pompeii, not by the volcano itself, but by the ordinary morning it destroyed. People were baking bread, planning weddings, and packing for voyages, never knowing the mountain above them was about to explode.

This is the dramatic true story of the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD: the seventeen-year-old boy whose letters are our only eyewitness account, his heroic uncle who sailed into the ash cloud to save strangers, and the city that was frozen in time for nearly two thousand years.
